queries.name: open_incident
queries.cypher:
// purpose: Open the incident for an alert (idempotent). The incident is the shared board every agent reads and writes.
MATCH (a:Alert {id: $alert_id})-[:FIRED_ON]->(s:Service)
MERGE (i:Incident {id: $incident_id})
ON CREATE SET i.status = 'open', i.opened_at = a.at, i.symptom = a.symptom, i.title = a.name
MERGE (i)-[:TRIGGERED_BY]->(a)
MERGE (i)-[:IMPACTS {hops: 0}]->(s)
RETURN i.id AS incident, i.status AS status, s.id AS service, a.at AS at, a.symptom AS symptom, a.name AS alert

queries.name: recall_similar
queries.cypher:
// purpose: Episodic recall by structure, not text: resolved incidents whose root-cause service is on the alerting service's live dependency path. Same symptom scores higher.
MATCH (i:Incident {id: $incident_id})-[:TRIGGERED_BY]->(a:Alert)-[:FIRED_ON]->(o:Service)
MATCH (past:Incident {status: 'resolved'})-[:CAUSED_BY]->(c:Change)-[:CHANGED]->(s:Service)
WHERE past.opened_at < a.at AND past.id <> i.id
WITH o, s, a.at AS alert_at, a, past, c
CALL {
  // Live hops o -> s (same block as path_suspects, which explains it).
  WITH o, s, alert_at
  WITH o, s, alert_at, shortestPath((o)-[:DEPENDS_ON*0..6]->(s)) AS sp
  WHERE sp IS NOT NULL
  WITH o, s, alert_at, sp,
       all(r IN relationships(sp) WHERE r.valid_from <= alert_at AND (r.valid_to IS NULL OR r.valid_to > alert_at)) AS live
  OPTIONAL MATCH p = (o)-[e:DEPENDS_ON*0..6]->(s)
  WHERE NOT live AND e.valid_from <= alert_at AND (e.valid_to IS NULL OR e.valid_to > alert_at)
  WITH live, sp, min(length(p)) AS shortest_live
  WITH CASE WHEN live THEN length(sp) ELSE shortest_live END AS hops
  WHERE hops IS NOT NULL
  RETURN hops
}
OPTIONAL MATCH (past)-[:FIXED_WITH]->(rb:Runbook)
RETURN past.id AS incident, past.title AS title, past.symptom AS symptom, s.id AS cause_service,
       c.kind AS cause_kind, c.id AS cause_change, hops, rb.id AS runbook, rb.title AS runbook_title,
       2 + CASE WHEN past.symptom = a.symptom THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS score
ORDER BY score DESC, past.opened_at DESC
LIMIT 5

queries.name: memory_suspects
queries.cypher:
// purpose: Procedural memory decides: for each recalled incident, the runbook that fixed it names a service and a change kind; suspect in-window changes of that kind on that service, most trusted runbook first.
MATCH (i:Incident {id: $incident_id})-[:TRIGGERED_BY]->(a:Alert)-[:FIRED_ON]->(o:Service)
MATCH (i)-[x:RECALLS]->(past:Incident)-[:FIXED_WITH]->(rb:Runbook)-[:FOR_SERVICE]->(s:Service)
WHERE x.score >= $min_score
MATCH (c:Change {kind: rb.kind})-[:CHANGED]->(s)
WHERE c.at >= a.at - $window AND c.at <= a.at
WITH o, s, a.at AS alert_at, past, rb, c
CALL {
  // Live hops o -> s (same block as path_suspects, which explains it).
  WITH o, s, alert_at
  WITH o, s, alert_at, shortestPath((o)-[:DEPENDS_ON*0..6]->(s)) AS sp
  WHERE sp IS NOT NULL
  WITH o, s, alert_at, sp,
       all(r IN relationships(sp) WHERE r.valid_from <= alert_at AND (r.valid_to IS NULL OR r.valid_to > alert_at)) AS live
  OPTIONAL MATCH p = (o)-[e:DEPENDS_ON*0..6]->(s)
  WHERE NOT live AND e.valid_from <= alert_at AND (e.valid_to IS NULL OR e.valid_to > alert_at)
  WITH live, sp, min(length(p)) AS shortest_live
  WITH CASE WHEN live THEN length(sp) ELSE shortest_live END AS hops
  WHERE hops IS NOT NULL
  RETURN hops
}
RETURN c.id AS change, s.id AS service, c.kind AS kind, c.at AS at, hops,
       rb.id AS runbook, rb.title AS runbook_title, rb.successes AS successes, rb.uses AS uses,
       collect(DISTINCT past.id) AS recalled
ORDER BY toFloat(successes) / uses DESC, at DESC

anomalies_between
queries.cypher:
// purpose: Which of the given services showed an anomaly between the change and the alert.
UNWIND $services AS sid
MATCH (x:Anomaly)-[:ON]->(s:Service {id: sid})
WHERE x.at >= $since AND x.at <= $until
RETURN s.id AS service, min(x.at) AS first_at, collect(x.summary)[0] AS summary

queries.name: red_before
queries.cypher:
// purpose: The latest anomaly on a service between the start of the alert window and a change landing on it: was the service already failing before its own change (a cascade victim)?
MATCH (x:Anomaly)-[:ON]->(:Service {id: $service})
WHERE x.at >= $since AND x.at < $until
RETURN max(x.at) AS at

queries.name: record_evidence
queries.cypher:
// purpose: Attach a check's verdict as an Evidence node (SUPPORTS / REFUTES the hypothesis) and update the hypothesis status.
MATCH (h:Hypothesis {id: $hypothesis_id})
MERGE (e:Evidence {id: $evidence_id})
SET e.verdict = $verdict, e.reason = $reason, e.tag = $tag, e.path = $path, e.at = $at, e.explained = $explained
WITH h, e, h.status AS before
// A human-confirmed cause stays confirmed whatever a later re-check says.
SET h.status = CASE WHEN h.status = 'confirmed' THEN h.status WHEN $verdict = 'supports' THEN 'supported'
                    WHEN $verdict = 'refutes' THEN 'refuted' ELSE 'inconclusive' END,
    h.explained = $explained, h.onset = $onset, h.gaps = $gaps, h.red_before = $red_before
FOREACH (_ IN CASE WHEN $verdict = 'supports' THEN [1] ELSE [] END | MERGE (e)-[:SUPPORTS]->(h))
FOREACH (_ IN CASE WHEN $verdict = 'refutes' THEN [1] ELSE [] END | MERGE (e)-[:REFUTES]->(h))
WITH h, before
// Procedural memory learns from misses too: a runbook whose suggestion was refuted loses confidence (once).
OPTIONAL MATCH (rb:Runbook {id: h.runbook})
FOREACH (x IN CASE WHEN rb IS NOT NULL AND $verdict = 'refutes' AND before = 'open' THEN [rb] ELSE [] END |
  SET x.uses = x.uses + 1)
RETURN h.id AS hypothesis, h.status AS status

queries.name: who_knows
queries.cypher:
// purpose: Who knows a service, ranked by graph evidence: on the owning team (3), authored changes to it (2 each), was paged for it in an incident (1 each), wrote docs, tickets or chat that mention or decide it (1 each, at most 3: writing about a service supports hands-on evidence, never outweighs it).
MATCH (s:Service {id: $service})
MATCH (p:Person)-[:MEMBER_OF]->(t:Team)
WITH s, p, t,
     size([(s)<-[:OWNS]-(t) | 1]) AS owns,
     size(list.dedup([(s)<-[:CHANGED]-(c:Change)-[:AUTHORED_BY]->(p) | c.id])) AS changes,
     size(list.dedup([(i:Incident)-[pg:PAGED]->(p) WHERE pg.for_service = s.id | i.id])) AS incidents,
     size(list.dedup([(s)<-[:MENTIONS|DECIDES]-(x)-[:AUTHORED_BY]->(p) | x.id])) AS docs
WHERE owns + changes + incidents + docs > 0
RETURN p.id AS person, p.name AS name, p.handle AS handle, t.name AS team, owns > 0 AS on_owning_team,
       changes, incidents, docs, 3 * owns + 2 * changes + incidents + CASE WHEN docs > 3 THEN 3 ELSE docs END AS score
ORDER BY score DESC, name
LIMIT 5

MERGE (i)-[x:CONSULTED]->(p)
ON CREATE SET x.for_service = $service, x.score = $score

queries.name: update_facts
queries.cypher:
// purpose: Facts for the status update: impact, who was paged and consulted, the supported cause with its author and sources (ticket, chat), and the runbook memory used.
MATCH (i:Incident {id: $incident_id})-[:TRIGGERED_BY]->(a:Alert)
OPTIONAL MATCH (i)-[imp:IMPACTS]->(s0:Service)
WITH i, a, collect(DISTINCT {service: s0.id, via: imp.via}) AS impacts
OPTIONAL MATCH (i)-[:PAGED]->(p:Person)-[:MEMBER_OF]->(t:Team)
WITH i, a, impacts, collect(DISTINCT {name: p.name, handle: p.handle, team: t.name}) AS paged
OPTIONAL MATCH (i)-[cx:CONSULTED]->(x:Person)-[:MEMBER_OF]->(xt:Team)
WITH i, a, impacts, paged,
     collect(DISTINCT {id: x.id, name: x.name, handle: x.handle, team: xt.name, service: cx.for_service}) AS experts
OPTIONAL MATCH (i)-[:HAS_HYPOTHESIS]->(h:Hypothesis)-[:SUSPECTS]->(c:Change)-[:CHANGED]->(s:Service)
WHERE h.status IN ['confirmed', 'supported']
WITH i, a, impacts, paged, experts, h, c, s ORDER BY h.status
LIMIT 1
OPTIONAL MATCH (c)-[:AUTHORED_BY]->(author:Person)
OPTIONAL MATCH (src)-[:REQUESTED|MENTIONS]->(c)
// Suggest the runbook that led memory to this cause, or the one a human confirmed fixed this incident. A runbook
// that merely shares the service and change kind may fix a different failure (a full disk vs a connection limit).
OPTIONAL MATCH (rb:Runbook {id: h.runbook})
OPTIONAL MATCH (i)-[:FIXED_WITH]->(fx:Runbook)
WITH a, impacts, paged, experts, h, c, s, author, src, coalesce(rb, fx) AS rb
RETURN a.name AS alert, impacts, paged, experts, c.id AS change, c.summary AS change_summary,
       c.kind AS change_kind, s.id AS cause_service, h.status AS cause_status, h.gaps AS cause_gaps,
       author.name AS author, collect(DISTINCT src.id) AS sources,
       collect(DISTINCT {id: rb.id, title: rb.title, steps: rb.steps, successes: rb.successes,
                         uses: rb.uses}) AS runbooks

queries.name: post_update
queries.cypher:
// purpose: Post (or rewrite) the status update on the incident and link it to every node it cites; stale citations are dropped. Lookups are per label so the id indexes are used.
MATCH (i:Incident {id: $incident_id})
MERGE (m:Message {id: $message_id})
SET m.kind = 'status_update', m.channel = '#incidents', m.text = $text, m.at = $at
MERGE (i)-[:HAS_UPDATE]->(m)
WITH m
OPTIONAL MATCH (m)-[old:CITES]->()
DELETE old
WITH DISTINCT m
UNWIND $cites AS cid
OPTIONAL MATCH (c:Change {id: cid})
OPTIONAL MATCH (t:Ticket {id: cid})
OPTIONAL MATCH (msg:Message {id: cid})
OPTIONAL MATCH (rb:Runbook {id: cid})
OPTIONAL MATCH (p:Person {id: cid})
OPTIONAL MATCH (d:Doc {id: cid})
WITH m, coalesce(c, t, msg, rb, p, d) AS n
WHERE n IS NOT NULL
MERGE (m)-[:CITES]->(n)
RETURN count(n) AS cited
